propositions: The transition lib has a decoupled force interface (force: bool, reason: str, force_close: str) while claim has a unified force interface (force: str | None = None carrying the audit reason), causing inconsistency.
The transition CLI allows --reason to serve as the force-bypass audit note in addition to its close_reason role, unlike claim which uses only --force[=<reason>].
The in-memory force-bypass reason concept is spelled four different ways (force_reason, force_close, force_close_reason, force_plan_review) across transition and claim internals.
Transition must be refactored to use a unified force: str | None parameter matching claim's shape, with legacy force_close and force: bool calls mapped via deprecation aliases.
Both transition and claim CLI surfaces and all guidance text must standardize on the --force[=<reason>] pattern exclusively, removing any --reason-as-force-note fallback or dual-spelling hints.

Internal in-memory naming across transition_compute, transition.py, and claim_compute must be unified to force_reason, while the persisted status_data key force_close_reason is retained for backward compatibility.
